stem.text: The function g is differentiable for all real numbers, and selected values of g and its derivative are given in the table. Must there be a value c, with \( 1 < c < 8 \), for which \( g(c) = -5 \)? Justify your answer.

answer_key.label: No, because although g is differentiable on \( [1, 8] \), so it is continuous there, every tabulated value of g is greater than -5.

worked_solution.text: g is differentiable on \( [1, 8] \), so it is continuous there.
Every tabulated value of g is greater than -5, so no two of them have -5 between them.
The Intermediate Value Theorem guarantees nothing here, and g could stay greater than -5 on the whole interval, so no such c must exist.

options.label: Yes, such a c must exist, because g is continuous on \( [1, 8] \), so it is differentiable there, and the Intermediate Value Theorem applies.
options.derivation: the implication run backwards, continuity offered as the reason for differentiability, and the theorem then applied without its straddling condition
